Prevention: Clean tools and farm machinery to prevent tubers from being spread
Use certified clean seed to avoid weed seed introduction through contamination
Do not accept potentially contaminated materials, e.g. manure, mulch and soil on planting stock
Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
During field preparation, avoid ploughing through nutsedge infested areas to avoid spread of weed tubers
Monitoring: Erect, perennial sedge (30-60 cm high), with extensive underground network composed of tubers.
Tubers dark brown/black, irregular shaped, 1-2 cm long at maturity, with several buds.
Leaves linear with distinct midrib, 7 mm wide.
Inflorescence with several unequal 'branches', each 2-6 cm long, emerging from the tip of the stem; each with 3-8 purplish-brown flowerheads
Inspect fields every two weeks, in particular during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when found
Look out for it in wetlands and along waterways
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Plough during dry season to expose the tubers and rhizomes in the soil to be destroyed by dessication.
Hand- weed every 2-3 weeks until crop canopy forms: the weed is shade intolerant
Place organic mulch over areas where weed is expect to grow to provide temporary weed suppression
Plough and cover an infested area with a polyethylene sheet to destroy tubers and rhizomes in the dry season (soil solarization)
Tillage must be deep (>12cm) in order to disturb as many of the rhizomes as possible.
Do this under dry conditions so the exposed rhizomes dessicate.
Direct Control (Chemical): Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Glyhposate (360g per litre of active ingredient per hectare) as post-emergence at the flowering stage.
Repeated applications necessary within a season, or one application at the beginning of each season for over a number of years, to eliminate weed in an area
Sulfentrazone (100 to 280g per litre of active ingredient per hectare)
